status: rule frozen 2026-11-23 (Task 6): `sessionBenchLong` holds the rule and its hash, unapproved. No paid call is approved by this record until the owner approves that hash (approved, approvedBy owner, approvedAt, text). Design review (Task 2) and the owner decisions below.

ownerDecisions.decision: After rule f42e1fe0 (owner: "My objective is to objectively measure whether we should have WM or not. I also would like objectively conclude that whatever memory system we have is better than simple compaction or mem0"; on the proposal: "I agree. Go ahead as you suggested"). (1) Fix 1 is reverted: a user task request kept word for word stays out of WM batches (f42e1fe0: STM+WM-deterministic D2 18/27, D2R 3/6 against STM-only 26/27, 6/6); fixes 2-4 stay. (2) Benchmark version 3 and analysis v3: after dependents in tasks 111-150, and after scores a check only at or past STM-only's first pool overflow in its session plus 10 tasks; live G11 asks that at least half of a session's after dependents be scored, in 2 of 3 pilot sessions. (3) mem0 is a baseline beside memory-off-llm, read by the verdict's step 3; the no-overflow guardrail counts tasks that ended on an overflow on any arm (f42e1fe0's 4 mem0 overflows were compacted around by the kernel; all 150 tasks completed). (4) The dev sessions decide the configuration; the claims against memory-off-llm and mem0 are read once on held-out sessions under a later rule. The compaction baseline is the strongest of three: in the 218.3 screen (36 sessions, the same worker) memory-off-llm passed 281/384 tasks, claude-code-prompt 260, codex-prompt 218.

150 tasks per session, in 6 phases of 25 (benchmark version 2). Chosen with the Task 7 pilot's live measurement in view: on beam-free STM records 104.1 description tokens a task (97.3-116) and the pool first overflows at task 84 on average (75 densest, 90 sparsest), after every version-1 `after` dependent (tasks 64-100). Dependents in `before` stay at tasks 20-38, `after` moves to tasks 95-150, so 67 tasks run past the mean overflow and 56 fall in the `after` bucket. A smaller window and a product pool setting were the other options.

supersedes.decision: 100 tasks per session, in 4 phases of 25. Chosen with the measurement in view: the pool overflows at task 53 on average (39 densest, 70 sparsest), so 48% of the session runs under eviction and 37 tasks fall in the `after` bucket; eviction does not reach high records (the user's rules and changes) before about task 132. 125 tasks was the recommendation.

ownerDecisions.decision: 12 dev sessions, one run each: 4 per family, so the per-family draw is [4, 4, 4] of 12 (not the [6, 3, 3] the plan's Expected Outcome stated). At least 60 D2 and 60 D4 checks in the `after` bucket over the dev set. The pilot's spread replaces the detectable-effect estimate (about 14 points).
mem0 runs as a side arm: reported beside the decision arms, never read by the verdict.
ownerDecisions.text: Run mem0 as a side arm

ownerDecisions.decision: Task 6's three-way rule: keep WM on a lower bound > 0 with the control and cost guards, drop WM when both WM arms' upper bounds are under +5 points, the owner decides in between.
2.3B input tokens for the pilot and the full run under one hash: the upper-bound estimate of about 1.97B (1.64B decision arms, 0.23B mem0, 0.10B calibration) plus about 15% for jobs that rerun.

buckets.afterNote: Benchmark version 3 (owner, 2026-11-26): after above task 110 (version 2: above 94). The analysis (v3) scores an after check only at or past STM-only's measured first overflow in its session plus 10 tasks. byLength is the Task 7 version-2 measurement.

findings.text: The pool bound counts description tokens, but the block the request carries is larger.
Session memory sizes itself from the kernel's input cap (W minus the output reserve minus 1,024), not the provider wrapper's.
The mid-loop trigger counts 4 characters per token over messages and the summary; in window tokens with the fixed part, a request just under it is close to the cap.
Eviction leaves out the lowest relevance first. Word-for-word user messages and corrections are high, so until the high records alone pass the pool, only lower records are left out.
The rehearsal drop starts when active records pass its target. Its model is the session's unless rehearsal.model is set.
Word-for-word user messages, user statements and durable records alone reach the pool at this task: from there an order that protects them has nothing else to leave out.

product.note: the package's src after plan 218.5 Tasks 1, 3 and 7 (tests excluded); the kernel and providers are the tree's at the run. Task 7's fixes (owner, 2026-11-25): WM items count against the pool; link protections lapse after wm.protectRequestTasks (3) newer user requests; deterministic WM keeps only high or critical outcomes. The fourth, batching finished task requests kept word for word for WM, is reverted (owner, 2026-11-26): rule f42e1fe0 showed WM discarding the user's rules that ride inside task requests (STM+WM-deterministic D2 18/27, D2R 3/6 against STM-only's 26/27, 6/6)

rule.selection: every dev session (12: 4 per family; owner, Task 2), 150 tasks each (benchmark version 2; owner, Task 7, 2026-11-24: on the pilot's live rates the pool first overflowed at task 75-90, after every version-1 `after` dependent; version 3, owner 2026-11-26: `after` dependents in tasks 111-150, scored past STM-only's measured overflow plus 10 tasks); heldout-a and heldout-b stay unread. The pilot is the first dev session of each family in the label-blind order
rule.armsNote: each arm differs only in `memory` (arms.mjs). STM-only: the 0.14.0 defaults (WM off) with Task 1's fixes, context.eviction relevance; STM-only-protect: protect-user; STM+WM: WM on, model policy, each phase's scope through memory:scope; STM+WM-deterministic: the same, deterministic policy; mem0: memory-off-llm plus mem0's retrieval as a context block; a baseline with memory-off-llm (owner, 2026-11-26: it was the side arm, Task 2), read by the verdict's step 3

calibration.text: amnesic (the floor: a fresh session per task) and oracle-notes (the ceiling: memory-off-llm plus every dependency's current evidence) on the 3 pilot sessions

wm.text: both WM arms pin wm.triggerTokens 3,000 (one wm.batchTokens batch per pass; Task 3 finding 1). At the product default 10,000 WM's first pass comes at about task 89, after the pool overflows at about task 53. Offline (Task 5) the first pass comes at task 33-34, 2-4 passes per session. Live G11 applies to the STM arms only; the WM arms report their first pass and whether the pool overflowed. Benchmark version 2 (Task 7): live STM records about two thirds of the offline rate, so the pool first overflows at about task 84 (75-90) and the WM trigger fires later than these offline numbers; 3,000 stays, so WM still passes well before the overflow

rule.rehearsal: no arm runs the Rehearsal drop: the memory system turns it on only when wm and ltm are both on, and no arm turns ltm on (Task 5 finding 1); the rows count the drops (0 expected)
rule.modelChoice: the main agent on hy4-flash-free, as in the screen (rule a1c6df8d, plan 218.3 Task 12); every memory worker (STM, WM, LLM-compaction summaries, Mem0) on muse-spark-1.3-contributor at reasoning low, the same worker for every arm, as in the screen. Task 7 history: muse-spark failed about 1 worker call in 30-100 on the first smoke job (an upstream 400 before the answer, now resent by upstreamRetryFetch; an upstream server_error mid-stream), so the owner moved to beam-free (2026-11-24); beam-free hit its free daily allowance after about 2,950 calls (429 rate_limit_error, retry-after about 9.7 hours) in rule 0d6beef6's calibration; the owner moved to deepseek-v4.1-flash (paid), which answered tool calls in 10-35 s (p50 21.5 s, 29-58 reasoning tokens: gateway latency, not thinking). Owner, 2026-11-24: "Let's try muse spark 1.2 or 1.3 contributor". In a 12-call parallel tool-call probe at reasoning low: muse-spark-1.3-contributor 12 of 12, p50 4.7 s, max 6.6 s; 1.2 12 of 12, p50 4.4 s, max 4.9 s. 1.3 is chosen: it was the screen's worker and its v3 ledgers are the Task 2 design measurement
rule.samplingNote: the screen's: temperature 0; the agent at thinkingLevel low; one tool call per main-agent turn (the harness answers the others with a fixed text); workerReasoningEffort low; workerOutput window (a worker call may write what W leaves after its input)
rule.outputNote: Task 7 (owner, 2026-11-24): the main agent reserves 16,384 output tokens and its model window is the input cap plus that (46,336); the input cap stays W minus 2,048 (29,952), so the pool (8,678), the kept tail, the mid-loop trigger, the job sizes and G11 are the design's. The memory worker keeps W 32,000, 2,048 by default and its workerOutput room. Why: on rule c2e39021 hy4-flash-free at thinking low spent the whole 2,048 on reasoning on hard turns and ended the task with no answer (oracle-notes 54.7%); resent at 4,096, 8,192 and 16,384, 2, 1 and 0 of the 4 capped turns still hit the cap (most reasoning 12,061). The owner kept thinking low (thinking none is not real-world use). The per-task limits stay (60,000 output tokens a task)
rule.limitsNote: the screen's live limits: maxToolCalls and maxTurns 60 for every arm

embedder.runtime: llama.cpp llama-server, Vulkan backend (RADV), GPU offload of every layer
embedder.device: the discrete GPU (AMD Radeon RX 6550M, RADV NAVI24, 4 GB): the Vulkan device whose name matches /NAVI ?24/i
embedder.deviation: Mem0's default embedder is OpenAI text-embedding-3-small; Gemini's free tier (Task 11) caps at 1,000 requests a day, so the owner chose a local embedder (2026-11-19) and then BGE-M3 for retrieval quality, on the GPU through llama.cpp/Vulkan: recorded as a G10 deviation

rule.embedderNote: mem0's embedder is the screen's: BGE-M3 on llama.cpp (Vulkan), local
rule.ceilingBasis: owner, Task 2: 2.3B input tokens (cached included) across every usage log under the run's wire directory, for the pilot and the full run under one hash; no new job starts at or above it, jobs in flight finish
rule.faults: the screen's: a 429/5xx/transport answer that outlasts the patient retries waits 15 minutes inside the request and is sent again (quota waits never fail a task); a job a provider error still reaches is a fault: no row, wait 15 minutes, the session runs again from its start. Task 7 (owner, 2026-11-23: the run must survive model call failures and an internet outage): a job whose provider setup fails for any reason but a credential, model or provider error (the catalog fetch timing out, the network down) is a provider fault too, never a dropped job; a stage that ends with a job missing is a restart (exit 6, the unit restarts and resumes from the rows), never a guardrail read off missing rows; a 400 that names an upstream failure ("Upstream request failed") is sent again up to 3 times (5 s, 20 s, 60 s) before it reaches the run (upstreamRetryFetch), and one that still refuses reasoning_effort is sent once more without it (Task 7, 2026-11-25: muse-spark's four-times-running refusal faulted two pilot jobs and a smoke job); every provider request turns the kernel's 60 s connect timeout off (withoutConnectTimeout), because it wraps the whole injected fetch and cut every wait above at 60 s; stallGuardFetch's 300 s no-headers and idle guards stay
rule.workerFaults: the screen's (owner, 2026-11-21): a job with any memory-worker call that failed after every retry (meter.workerErrors), or any STM batch recorded without the model (meter.stmFallbacks), leaves no row and runs again; a job's third worker fault, or a provider's usage-limit answer, halts the run with STOP: for the owner. workerAborts are not faults
rule.overflow: the harness rejects a request over W's input cap as a provider would (context_overflow). That is the arm's scored outcome, as in the screen (the task fails, the row stays, meter.overflows counts it); it is not a fault, because a rerun would meet the same block and reach the third-fault stop. The pilot's live guardrail allows no task to end on an overflow (owner, 2026-11-26: rule f42e1fe0's mem0 arm met 4 overflows on one session and the kernel compacted and retried each, so all 150 tasks completed; the compaction vote counts the conversation and its summaries, not a host's context block such as mem0's). Overflows the kernel recovered are reported per arm. Task 5 finding 2: the WM arms' block is not bounded by the pool (16,217 rendered tokens offline, a worst request near 98.5% of the cap), so a WM arm can overflow where the STM arms do not
rule.controlNote: analysis v2 (owner, 2026-11-25): the control guard reads C-stable, the C checks of every job but count-errors (score.mjs NOISY_JOBS); C and task keep every job. Analysis v3 (owner, 2026-11-26): after scores a check only at or past STM-only's first pool overflow in its session plus 10 tasks (score.mjs pressureTasksFrom); mem0 is a baseline in step 3
order: pre-run: the offline guardrails G1-G11 pass with nothing pending (guardrails.mjs); the gate approves this hash

smoke: memory-off-llm on the smallest pilot session, alone; no fault, no task failed outside the arm's outcomes, and a projected total within the ceiling; a miss stops the run. Provider errors the retries absorbed (a stream cut mid-answer and sent again) are reported, not a miss (owner, 2026-11-25: rule aeb684e0's smoke met one such cut at exchange 375 of the main model, and the strict rule would have stopped the run on a task that passed)

calibration: amnesic and oracle-notes on the pilot sessions; oracle-notes passes >= 60% of tasks and amnesic fails >= 70% of D2 and D2R and >= 60% of D4 (owner, 2026-11-25: amnesic failed 70.4% then 63.0% of D4, the same 7 of 27 ship-day checks passing without memory both times), or the run stops

pilot: the decision arms on the pilot sessions; then live G11 (at least half of a session's after dependents sit at or past STM-only's first overflow plus 10 tasks, in >= 2 of 3 sessions) and no task ended on an overflow, or the run stops (Task 7)

the rest (Task 8, on the owner's word): the decision arms on the other 9 dev sessions; the pilot's rows count. The dev sessions decide the configuration; the claims against memory-off-llm and mem0 are read on held-out sessions under a later rule
rule.checkins: every 30 minutes and after every job: rows done, input tokens spent, projected total
rule.instrumentation: each memory-system row carries, per task, block tokens (rendered and description), active STM tokens, fullFold, records left out by relevance and how many were durable or user statements, Rehearsal drops, WM items, tombstones and passes; per dependent, whether its sources' records were in the block (ids only)

analysis.unit: check or task, paired by id across arms; sessions are the clusters
analysis.statistic: pairedClusterPermutation (scripts/memory-bench/stats.mjs): cluster bootstrap interval of the mean paired difference, sign-flip p
analysis.pooled: before and after pool D1-D4 only (same class mix in both buckets); D2R is its own metric (after only)
analysis.pressure: after (pooled, per class, and D2R) scores a check only at or past STM-only's first pool overflow in its session plus 10 tasks (pressureTasksFrom); a session where STM-only never overflowed scores no after check
analysis.control: C-stable: the C checks of every job but count-errors (NOISY_JOBS); every check row of class C carries its task's job
analysis.reported: every arm's scores per class and bucket, every comparison above on every metric, whole-run tokens per passed task, the pressure counts and the after checks each session scored, and the effect detectable at N

reference.text: STM-only-protect becomes the reference, and protect-user the eviction default, if it beats STM-only on after dependency checks (95% lower bound > 0) and its C-stable lower bound is > -5 points; otherwise the reference is STM-only

wm.cost: whole-run tokens (main and workers, input and output, plus embeddings) per passed task
wm.text: Each WM arm against the reference on after dependency checks, Holm-adjusted over the two WM arms. Keep WM if a WM arm's lower bound is > 0, its C-stable lower bound > -5 points and its whole-run tokens per passed task <= 1.5x the reference's (the best such arm sets WM's default policy under a host scope). Drop WM if both WM arms' upper bounds are < +5 points. Otherwise the owner decides

baselines.text: The reference against each baseline (memory-off-llm: LLM compaction; mem0) on after dependency checks, Holm-adjusted over the two baselines. The memory system beats a baseline if the reference's lower bound is > 0 and its C-stable lower bound > -5 points. Dev sessions decide the configuration only; the claim is read on held-out sessions (a later rule)

stmAtLength.text: if reference - memory-off-llm has a lower bound <= 0 on after while before's lower bound is > 0, the report sends a P1 STM finding to the owner
